newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Salomon starts offering Philippine yankee bonds.
newsitem.headline: Salomon starts offering Philippine yankee bonds.

text.p: Salomon Brothers has begun offering Philippine Yankee bonds in preparation for a possible launching later in the day in New York, senior bankers said on Tuesday.
The 30-year bonds are being offered at 185 basis points above the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, while the 100-year bonds are being offered at 197.5 basis points over, they said.
Bankers said Salomon Brothers was offering $400 million worth of 30-year and $100 million worth of 100-year bonds.
The pricing compares to a current quoted spread for the Philippine 20-year Brady exchange bond of 180 bp.
Earlier in the day, Salomon Brothers won a fresh mandate from the Philippine Central Bank as firm underwriter for the maiden yankee bond offering.
The investment bank had headed a group of lead mangers for the initial planned offering, but that deal was postponed in April by the Central Bank which blamed poor market conditions.
Manila eventually called for a fresh round of bids, which closed on Tuesday morning.
Salomon Brothers local office declined to comment on the price of their winning bid which some bankers said was very low to make up for the problems in the initial attempts to issue the bond.
There have been widespread reports of infighting among the original lead managers, though Philippine Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said "many" were not true.
